question: Who among the following Indian women shuttlers is the runner-up in the Madrid Spain Masters-2023 tournament?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PV Sindhu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• PV Sindhu was the runner-up at the Madrid Spain Masters 2023 (a BWF World Tour Super 300 event), losing the women's singles final to Indonesia's Gregoria Mariska Tunjung in straight sets on 2 April 2023. (मैड्रिड स्पेन मास्टर्स 2023 — पीवी सिंधु उपविजेता)

 

• PV Sindhu is a two-time Olympic medallist (Silver at Rio 2016, Bronze at Tokyo 2020) and a former BWF World Champion (2019), and remains India's most decorated woman badminton player.

 

• On her way to the final at Madrid, Sindhu defeated Singapore's Yeo Jia Min in the semi-final.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Saina Nehwal is another leading Indian shuttler and a Rio 2016 Olympic bronze medallist, but she did not contest this final.

 

• BWF World Tour events are ranked Super 100 to Super 1000 by prize money and ranking points; the Spain Masters was a Super 300 event in 2023.

 

NOTE

 

• Saina Nehwal (Option 1): A former World No. 1 and Olympic medallist, but not the finalist at this tournament.

 

• Jwala Gutta (Option 2): Primarily a doubles specialist; she was not part of this event's singles final.

 

• Neha Gurudutt (Option 4): Not connected with the Madrid Spain Masters 2023 final.

question: Which of the following sentences is INCORRECT with regard to government budget?
option_1: Government budget is a constitutional requirement in India.
option_2: It is a statement of estimated receipts and expenditures of the government for the financial year.
option_4: It is a statement of receipts and expenditures incurred by the government.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is a statement of receipts and expenditures incurred by the government.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A government budget is, by definition, a statement of the estimated (anticipated) receipts and expenditure of the government for a coming financial year — not a record of amounts already incurred. (सरकारी बजट — अनुमानित प्राप्तियाँ और व्यय)

 

• Because Option 4 describes the budget as recording expenditure already incurred (i.e., actual, past spending) rather than estimated future spending, it misstates the fundamental nature of a budget and is therefore the incorrect statement.

 

• The budget is indeed a constitutional requirement: under Article 112, the President must have an Annual Financial Statement laid before both Houses of Parliament each year, so Option 1 is correct (not the answer).

 

• It genuinely comprises two main accounts — the Revenue Budget and the Capital Budget — so Option 3 is also a correct statement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Union Budget is presented in Parliament, typically on 1 February, by the Finance Minister.

 

• The Budget also distinguishes between Revenue Receipts/Expenditure and Capital Receipts/Expenditure, forming the basis of the Revenue and Capital accounts.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Correct statement — the budget is mandated by Article 112 of the Constitution.

 

• Option 2: Correct statement — the budget is precisely a statement of estimated receipts and expenditure for a financial year.

 

• Option 3: Correct statement — the budget comprises the Revenue Account and the Capital Account.

question: Which of the following teams won the 15th edition of the Indian Premier League cricket tournament in the year 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat Titans.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gujarat Titans, captained by Hardik Pandya, won the IPL 2022 (15th edition) title in their debut season, defeating Rajasthan Royals in the final. (गुजरात टाइटन्स — आईपीएल 2022 विजेता)

 

• The final was played on 29 May 2022 at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad.

 

• Gujarat Titans became only the third team (after Rajasthan Royals in 2008 and Mumbai Indians) to win the IPL title in its debut season.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hardik Pandya was named captain of Gujarat Titans for their inaugural season and led them to the title.

 

• Jos Buttler (Rajasthan Royals) won the Orange Cap and Yuzvendra Chahal won the Purple Cap in IPL 2022.

 

NOTE

 

• Chennai Super Kings (Option 1): A record five-time IPL champion, but finished at the bottom of the points table in the 2022 season.

 

• Delhi Capitals (Option 3): Did not qualify for the IPL 2022 playoffs.

 

• Mumbai Indians (Option 4): A record five-time IPL champion, but had a poor 2022 season and did not qualify for the playoffs.

question: Which law was developed in the 1600s to describe that any force applied to a confined fluid is transmitted equally in all directions, regardless of the shape of the container?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pascal's Law.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pascal's Law, formulated by French scientist Blaise Pascal in the 17th century (1600s), states that pressure applied to an enclosed, incompressible fluid is transmitted equally and undiminished in all directions, regardless of the shape of the container. (पास्कल का नियम — द्रव में दाब का समान संचरण)

 

• This principle explains why pressure at any point in a static fluid depends only on depth and density, not on the shape of the vessel.

 

• Pascal's Law is the working principle behind hydraulic machines such as hydraulic lifts, hydraulic brakes, and hydraulic presses, which use fluid pressure to multiply force.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SI unit of pressure, the pascal (Pa), is named in honour of Blaise Pascal.

 

• Pascal also made major contributions to probability theory and built one of the earliest mechanical calculators.

 

NOTE

 

• Magnus's Law (Option 1): Relates to the Magnus effect, the force experienced by a spinning object moving through a fluid (used to explain the curved flight of a spinning ball).

 

• Graham's Law (Option 2): States that the rate of effusion/diffusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its molar mass.

 

• Torricelli's Law (Option 4): Relates the speed of fluid flowing out of an orifice to the height of fluid above the opening; also associated with the invention of the barometer.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution enshrines that if we are observing any religious procession, then we need to remember communal harmony?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 51A (e).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 51A(e), one of the Fundamental Duties under Part IVA of the Constitution, casts a duty on every citizen "to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities." (अनुच्छेद 51ए(ई) — सामाजिक और सांप्रदायिक सद्भाव)

 

• This duty is understood to require citizens to maintain communal harmony in situations such as religious processions, festivals, and other community events where communal sensitivities may arise.

 

• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, based on the Soviet-style duties model.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties listed under Article 51A (Articles 51A(a) to 51A(k)); the last one, 51A(k), on the duty to provide education, was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, i.e., they cannot be enforced by courts, unlike Fundamental Rights.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 51A(d) (Option 1): Duty "to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so."

 

• Article 51A(c) (Option 2): Duty "to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India."

 

• Article 51A(b) (Option 3): Duty "to cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom."

question: Which state in India has the highest literacy rate as per Census of 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of 2011, Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate in India at 93.91%, retaining a position it has held since Census 1991. (केरल — सर्वाधिक साक्षरता दर)

 

• Kerala's high literacy is credited to sustained investment in public education, high female literacy, and social reform movements dating back to the erstwhile princely states of Travancore and Cochin.

 

• Bihar recorded the lowest literacy rate in the country as per Census 2011, at 61.8%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's overall literacy rate as per Census 2011 was 74.04% (male 82.14%, female 65.46%).

 

• Among Union Territories, Lakshadweep recorded the highest literacy rate in Census 2011.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar (Option 1): Recorded the lowest literacy rate among Indian states in Census 2011.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 2): Had a literacy rate of around 82.3%, well above the national average but far below Kerala's.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 4): Had a literacy rate of around 80.1%, also below Kerala's.

question: 'Safeguarding India's Intangible Cultural Heritage and Diverse Cultural Traditions of India' is a scheme of which Ministry of the Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Culture.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The "Scheme for Safeguarding the Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) and Diverse Cultural Traditions of India" is administered by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India. (संस्कृति मंत्रालय — अमूर्त सांस्कृतिक धरोहर योजना)

 

• The scheme aims to identify, document, protect, and promote India's rich and diverse intangible cultural heritage, including oral traditions, performing arts, social practices, rituals, festive events, and traditional craftsmanship, in line with UNESCO's 2003 Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage, which India ratified in 2005.

 

• Under this scheme, the Ministry also supports the nomination of Indian elements to UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ministry of Culture also runs other schemes such as the Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Peace and Non-Violence and administers institutions like the Sangeet Natak Akademi, Sahitya Akademi, and Lalit Kala Akademi.

 

• India currently has multiple elements inscribed on UNESCO's ICH list, including Durga Puja, Kumbh Mela, Yoga, and Garba of Gujarat.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Tourism (Option 2): Focuses on tourism promotion and infrastructure, not intangible heritage safeguarding.

 

• Ministry of Education (Option 3): Responsible for the education sector, not this heritage scheme.

 

• Ministry of Urban Development (Option 4): Deals with urban infrastructure and housing, unrelated to this scheme.

question: In which of the following states did NABARD launch the EShakti project for the first time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand and Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• NABARD's E-Shakti project, launched in 2015, is a pilot initiative for the digitisation of Self-Help Group (SHG) accounts, and was first rolled out in Ramgarh district (Jharkhand) and Dhule district (Maharashtra). (ई-शक्ति परियोजना — झारखंड और महाराष्ट्र)

 

• The project aims to bring SHG members under the ambit of financial inclusion by digitising their savings and credit data, improving access to credit and reducing bookkeeping errors.

 

• Following the success of the pilot, e-Shakti was later scaled up to over 100 districts across 28 states and Union Territories.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) was established in 1982 and is India's apex development bank for agriculture and rural development.

 

• NABARD also runs the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme (SBLP), one of the largest microfinance programmes in the world.

 

NOTE

 

• West Bengal and Assam (Option 1): Not the states where the e-Shakti pilot was first launched.

 

• Uttar Pradesh and Punjab (Option 3): Not the states where the e-Shakti pilot was first launched.

 

• Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): Not the states where the e-Shakti pilot was first launched.

question: Alha and Udal, who gave stiff resistance to the enemy, belonged to which of the following Rajput States?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandella.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alha and Udal were legendary warrior brothers and generals who served under the Chandela (Chandella) king Parmardi Dev (Parmal) of Mahoba, and are celebrated for their fierce resistance against invaders, especially in the famous folk epic "Alha-Khand." (आल्हा-ऊदल — चंदेल वंश)

 

• The Chandela dynasty ruled the Bundelkhand region (present-day parts of Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh) between roughly the 9th and 13th centuries CE, with Khajuraho as their most renowned architectural legacy.

 

• Alha and Udal are remembered in folk tradition for their valour in battles against rivals such as Prithviraj Chauhan, and the ballad describing their exploits remains a part of oral tradition in North India even today.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chandela rulers are credited with building the famous Khajuraho temples, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, under rulers like Yashovarman and Dhanga.

 

• The Chandela dynasty also built the Kalinjar Fort, an important hill fortress in present-day Uttar Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Parmar (Option 1): A Rajput dynasty that ruled Malwa, with Dhar and Ujjain as important centres; notable ruler was Raja Bhoj.

 

• Kalchuri (Option 2): A dynasty that ruled parts of central India, including areas around Tripuri (near Jabalpur) and later the Kalyani-Kalachuris of the Deccan.

 

• Gahadavala (Option 4): A dynasty that ruled the Kannauj region; notable ruler was Govindachandra, and the dynasty fell to Muhammad Ghori's forces under Jayachandra.

question: In 1996, Dr. Indira PP Bora, an exponent of Sattriya, was honoured with the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. Indira P.P. Bora, a renowned exponent and pioneering promoter of Sattriya dance (the classical dance form of Assam), was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1996. (इंदिरा पीपी बोरा — सत्रिया नृत्य)

 

• Sattriya is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originating in the Vaishnavite monasteries (sattras) of Assam, founded by the saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardev in the 15th-16th century.

 

• Dr. Bora was later also honoured with the Padma Shri in 2020 for her contribution to Sattriya dance and its recognition as a classical dance form.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance, and drama, confers its awards ("Akademi Puraskar") as one of the highest honours for performing artists in the country.

 

• Sattriya was officially recognised as a classical dance form of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in the year 2000.

 

NOTE

 

• Filmfare Award (Option 1): Given for excellence in Hindi cinema; unrelated to classical dance.

 

• Bharat Ratna (Option 2): India's highest civilian award, not what Dr. Bora received in 1996.

 

• Saraswati Samman (Option 4): A literary award given for outstanding prose or poetry, not a performing arts honour.

question: Bokajan is a cement plant located in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bokajan is home to a major cement plant operated by the Cement Corporation of India (CCI), located in the Karbi Anglong district of Assam. (बोकाजान सीमेंट संयंत्र — असम)

 

• The Bokajan Cement Factory is one of the oldest and most important cement production units in the North-East India region.

 

• The plant draws limestone from nearby deposits and has historically been a significant industrial establishment for the region's development.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important industries in Assam include oil refineries (Digboi, Guwahati, Bongaigaon, Numaligarh) and tea processing units, given Assam's status as a leading tea-producing state.

 

• Digboi, in Assam, is home to Asia's oldest oil refinery.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar (Option 1): Not the location of the Bokajan cement plant.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Home to several cement plants (e.g., Satna), but not Bokajan.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): A major cement-producing state, but Bokajan is not located there.

question: Which of the following aggregates best describes the National Income?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NNP at FC.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• National Income, in the strict conventional sense used in Indian economic statistics, is defined as the Net National Product at Factor Cost (NNP at FC). (राष्ट्रीय आय — एनएनपी एट एफसी)

 

• It is derived by taking Gross National Product (GNP), subtracting depreciation (to get Net National Product) and adjusting for net indirect taxes (subtracting indirect taxes and adding subsidies) to convert market prices into factor cost.

 

• NNP at FC represents the sum total of factor incomes (wages, rent, interest, and profit) earned by a country's normal residents, both within the country and abroad, during a year, and is therefore treated as the most precise measure of National Income.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• GDP (Gross Domestic Product) measures the value of goods and services produced within a country's domestic territory, regardless of who produces them.

 

• GNP (Gross National Product) = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA); NNP = GNP − Depreciation.

 

NOTE

 

• GDP at MP (Option 1): Measures domestic output at market prices; does not represent National Income and includes depreciation and indirect taxes.

 

• NDP at MP (Option 3): Net Domestic Product at Market Prices; still restricted to domestic territory and market prices, not National Income.

 

• GNP at FC (Option 4): Close, but still includes depreciation, which must be subtracted to arrive at National Income (NNP at FC).

question: Subha Mudgal is famous for which of the following music forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hindustani music.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Shubha Mudgal is a renowned Indian vocalist famous for her mastery of Hindustani classical music, and is also known for her work in semi-classical, thumri, and popular fusion music. (शुभा मुद्गल — हिंदुस्तानी संगीत)

 

• She has been honoured with the Padma Shri (in the field of Art/Music) by the Government of India for her contributions.

 

• She belongs to the Gwalior, Kirana, and Jaipur-Atrauli gharana traditions of Hindustani classical vocal music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hindustani classical music is the classical music tradition of North India, as distinguished from Carnatic music, the classical tradition of South India.

 

• Shubha Mudgal is also known for popular compositions like "Ab Ke Sawan", which brought her mainstream popularity in the 1990s.

 

NOTE

 

• Carnatic music (Option 1): The classical music tradition of South India; not Shubha Mudgal's genre.

 

• Reggae music (Option 2): A Jamaican music genre, unrelated to Shubha Mudgal.

 

• Hip hop music (Option 3): A modern urban music genre, unrelated to Shubha Mudgal.

question: In 1851, who discovered the phenomenon of Eddy currents which flow in closed loops within conductors in planes perpendicular to the magnetic field?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Leon Foucault.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• French physicist Léon Foucault discovered eddy currents in 1851, observing that a copper disc rotating near a magnet experienced resistance due to induced circulating currents within the metal. (एडी धाराएं — लियोन फूको)

 

• Eddy currents are loops of electrical current induced within conductors by a changing magnetic field, flowing in closed paths within planes perpendicular to the magnetic field, as per Faraday's Law of electromagnetic induction, and named for their resemblance to swirling water eddies.

 

• Eddy currents are also referred to as Foucault currents in honour of their discoverer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Léon Foucault is also famous for the Foucault pendulum, a device demonstrating the Earth's rotation, and for measuring the speed of light with high precision.

 

• Eddy currents have practical applications in induction heating, electromagnetic braking, and metal detectors, though they cause undesirable energy loss in transformer cores (minimised by laminating the core).

 

NOTE

 

• David Hughes (Option 1): Known for early work on the microphone and wireless transmission, not the discovery of eddy currents.

 

• Charles Townes (Option 2): Co-inventor of the maser and laser, a 20th-century physicist unrelated to this 1851 discovery.

 

• Nicola Tesla (Option 3): Renowned for work on alternating current (AC) systems and induction motors, but not the discoverer of eddy currents.

question: What is the name of a type of waterfall with an enormous volume of water?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cataract.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A cataract is the term used for a large, powerful waterfall carrying an enormous volume of water, typically over a steep drop. (जलप्रपात — कैटरैक्ट)

 

• Well-known examples of cataracts include the Cataracts of the Nile in Africa, historically important for navigation and geography.

 

• The term is distinguished from smaller-scale terms like cascade or chute, which describe waterfalls with comparatively modest flow or a series of small drops.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• A cascade refers to a series of small waterfalls, one following another, typically over rocky terraces.

 

• The largest waterfalls by water volume in the world include Niagara Falls (North America) and Victoria Falls (Africa).

 

NOTE

 

• Cascade (Option 1): Refers to a small waterfall, or a series of small falls, not a large-volume waterfall.

 

• Rapid (Option 2): Refers to a fast-flowing, turbulent stretch of a river, not technically a waterfall.

 

• Chute (Option 4): Refers to a waterfall that flows through a narrow, steep channel, generally not associated with enormous volume.

question: Indian Councils Act of ______, also called Morley-Minto Reforms, series of reform measures enacted in the British Parliament
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1909.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Councils Act of 1909, popularly known as the Morley-Minto Reforms, was named after Lord Morley (Secretary of State for India) and Lord Minto (Viceroy of India). (मॉर्ले-मिंटो सुधार — 1909)

 

• It introduced separate electorates for Muslims, a highly significant and controversial provision that laid the groundwork for later communal representation in Indian politics.

 

• The Act also expanded the size of legislative councils at the Centre and in provinces, and allowed limited association of Indians with the executive councils of the Viceroy and Governors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) introduced dyarchy in the provinces.

 

• The Government of India Act, 1935 introduced provincial autonomy and proposed an All-India Federation (which never materialised).

 

NOTE

 

• 1919 (Option 2): Year of the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (Government of India Act, 1919), not the Morley-Minto Reforms.

 

• 1862 (Option 3): Year of an earlier Indian Councils Act that established legislative councils but not the Morley-Minto Reforms.

 

• 1935 (Option 4): Year of the Government of India Act, 1935, which introduced provincial autonomy.

question: Hornbill festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaland.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Hornbill Festival is the flagship cultural festival of Nagaland, held every year from 1 to 10 December at the Naga Heritage Village, Kisama, near Kohima. (हॉर्नबिल महोत्सव — नागालैंड)

 

• It is popularly called the "Festival of Festivals" because it brings together all the major Naga tribes on a single platform to showcase their traditions, dances, crafts, and cuisine.

 

• The festival is named after the hornbill bird, which holds a significant place in Naga tribal culture and folklore.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The festival is timed to coincide with Nagaland's Statehood Day, celebrated on 1 December.

 

• Other important tribal festivals include Sekrenyi (Angami tribe) and Moatsu (Ao tribe), both also from Nagaland.

 

NOTE

 

• Manipur (Option 2): Known for festivals like Yaoshang and Lai Haraoba, not the Hornbill Festival.

 

• Sikkim (Option 3): Known for festivals like Losar and Saga Dawa, not the Hornbill Festival.

 

• Assam (Option 4): Known for festivals like Bihu, not the Hornbill Festival.

question: Which country came out with the first 'official' compilation of volleyball rules and was published by the YMCA?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The US.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Volleyball was invented in 1895 by William G. Morgan, a physical education instructor at the YMCA in Holyoke, Massachusetts, USA. (वॉलीबॉल नियम — संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका)

 

• The first 'official' compilation of volleyball rules was published in the United States by the YMCA, formalising the sport that Morgan had originally called "Mintonette."

 

• The name "volleyball" was adopted because the ball was volleyed back and forth over a net.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The International Volleyball Federation (FIVB), the sport's global governing body, was founded in 1947, headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.

 

• Volleyball became an official Olympic sport at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.

 

NOTE

 

• Germany (Option 1): Not the origin of volleyball or its first official rules.

 

• The UK (Option 3): Not the origin of volleyball or its first official rules.

 

• Australia (Option 4): Not the origin of volleyball or its first official rules.

question: Velocity of circulation of money is ____________.
option_1: k times the value of transactions
option_2: the number of times a unit of money changes hands during the unit period
option_3: the number of times the same transactions can be repeated by a given volume of money supply
option_4: the ratio of money balance to the value of transactions
solution_text:
The correct answer is the number of times a unit of money changes hands during the unit period.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The velocity of circulation of money refers to the number of times one unit of money (e.g., one rupee) changes hands, i.e., is used in transactions, during a given period (usually a year). (मुद्रा परिसंचरण वेग — मुद्रा के हाथ बदलने की गति)

 

• It is a key component of the Quantity Theory of Money, expressed as MV = PT (or MV = PY), where M is money supply, V is velocity of circulation, P is the price level, and T (or Y) is the volume of transactions/output.

 

• A higher velocity of circulation means each unit of currency is being used more frequently, reflecting higher transaction activity relative to the money supply.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The concept of velocity of money was central to the classical Quantity Theory of Money, developed and refined by economists like Irving Fisher.

 

• Fisher's equation of exchange is written as MV = PT, linking money supply and velocity to the price level and transaction volume.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (k times the value of transactions): Confuses the concept with the Cambridge cash-balance approach, where 'k' represents the fraction of income held as money, not the definition of velocity itself.

 

• Option 3: Incorrectly frames velocity as being about repeating transactions using a fixed money supply, rather than the frequency with which a unit of money changes hands.

 

• Option 4: Describes a ratio of money balance to transaction value, which does not correctly define velocity of circulation.

question: Which of these is NOT true about green revolution?
option_1: It was funded by international agencies.
option_2: It was a private-sector programme for agricultural modernization.
option_3: It was targeted mainly in the wheat and rice-growing areas.
option_4: It was introduced only in areas that had assured irrigation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It was a private-sector programme for agricultural modernization.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Green Revolution in India, launched in the mid-1960s, was primarily a government-led, public-sector initiative, not a private-sector programme, making this the statement that is NOT true. (हरित क्रांति — सरकार समर्थित कार्यक्रम)

 

• It was spearheaded by agricultural scientist M.S. Swaminathan, with support from the Indian government and international agencies, and involved the introduction of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilisers, and irrigation.

 

• It was indeed supported/funded in part by international agencies (like the Ford Foundation and Rockefeller Foundation), was concentrated in wheat and rice-growing regions (notably Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh), and was largely confined to areas with assured irrigation, since HYV seeds required controlled water supply.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution significantly boosted India's wheat production, helping the country move toward food self-sufficiency by the early 1970s.

 

• The Green Revolution is often criticised for widening regional disparities, since it largely bypassed rain-fed, non-irrigated areas.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: A true statement — international agencies did provide funding and technical support for the Green Revolution.

 

• Option 3: A true statement — the Green Revolution was targeted mainly at wheat and rice-growing areas.

 

• Option 4: A true statement — the programme was largely restricted to areas with assured irrigation facilities.

question: The traditional 'Cheraw' dance, in which bamboo is used, is famous in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mizoram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Cheraw dance, popularly known as the "Bamboo Dance," is the most famous traditional folk dance of Mizoram. (चेरॉ नृत्य — मिज़ोरम)

 

• In this dance, pairs of dancers rhythmically tap, open, and close horizontal bamboo poles on the ground while other dancers step in and out of the poles in time with the beat.

 

• The Cheraw dance is one of the oldest folk dances of the Mizo people and is traditionally performed on festive and ceremonial occasions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable dances of Mizoram include Khuallam and Chailam.

 

• The bamboo dance tradition is also found among certain other Northeast Indian and Southeast Asian communities under different regional names.

 

NOTE

 

• Goa (Option 2): Known for folk dances like Fugdi and Dekhni, not the Cheraw dance.

 

• Odisha (Option 3): Known for dances like Odissi and Ghumura, not the Cheraw dance.

 

• Bihar (Option 4): Known for folk dances like Jat-Jatin, not the Cheraw dance.

question: Which of the following posts of Defence Research Development Organisation (DRDO) is in the Level I (top level) of its organisational chart?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Secretary DD and R & D.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the very top of DRDO's organisational chart (Level I) sits the Secretary, Department of Defence Research & Development (DDR&D), who also serves as the Chairman of DRDO and the Scientific Adviser to the Raksha Mantri (Defence Minister). (डीआरडीओ — रक्षा अनुसंधान एवं विकास सचिव)

 

• Below this top post, DRDO's structure includes Director Generals (DGs) heading various technical clusters, followed by Directors of individual laboratories, forming subsequent levels of the hierarchy.

 

• DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation), headquartered in New Delhi, functions under the Ministry of Defence and operates a network of laboratories across India engaged in defence-related research.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• DRDO was formed in 1958 by merging the Technical Development Establishment and the Directorate of Technical Development & Production with the Defence Science Organisation.

 

• DRDO has developed major indigenous defence systems such as the Agni and Prithvi missiles, Tejas Light Combat Aircraft, and the Arjun Main Battle Tank.

 

NOTE

 

• Director General Technical Cluster (Option 1): A senior post, but ranks below the Secretary DDR&D in the organisational hierarchy (Level II, not Level I).

 

• Director General Corporate (Option 3): Also a senior post below the top level of the DRDO hierarchy.

 

• Director of Laboratory (Option 4): Heads an individual DRDO laboratory, placed further down the organisational hierarchy.

question: The first-ever terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues were:
solution_text:
The correct answer is pteridophyta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pteridophytes (ferns and their allies) were the first vascular plants (tracheophytes) to colonise land, evolving specialised conducting tissues — xylem and phloem — for transporting water and nutrients. (टेरिडोफाइटा — प्रथम संवहनी पौधे)

 

• The development of vascular tissue allowed pteridophytes to grow taller and thrive independently of constantly moist environments, unlike earlier non-vascular land plants.

 

• Pteridophytes reproduce via spores and do not produce seeds or flowers, marking an evolutionary stage between non-vascular plants (bryophytes) and seed-bearing plants (gymnosperms and angiosperms).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common examples of pteridophytes include ferns, horsetails (Equisetum), and club mosses (Lycopodium).

 

• The evolutionary sequence of major plant groups is broadly: Algae → Bryophytes → Pteridophytes → Gymnosperms → Angiosperms.

 

NOTE

 

• Lichens (Option 2): Not plants at all, but a symbiotic association between fungi and algae/cyanobacteria; they lack vascular tissue.

 

• Bryophyta (Option 3): The first land plants but non-vascular, lacking specialised conducting tissue (e.g., mosses, liverworts).

 

• Algae (Option 4): Predominantly aquatic organisms, lacking true vascular tissue and not classified as terrestrial plants.

question: Bailadila range of hills are famous for which of the following minerals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iron ore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bailadila range of hills, located in the Dantewada district of Chhattisgarh, is one of India's richest and most important sources of high-grade iron ore. (बैलाडीला पहाड़ियाँ — लौह अयस्क)

 

• The iron ore mines here are operated by NMDC (National Mineral Development Corporation) and are among the largest mechanised iron ore mining operations in Asia.

 

• Iron ore extracted from Bailadila is exported (notably via Vishakhapatnam port) and also supplies major domestic steel plants.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major iron ore belts in India include the Bellary-Hospet region (Karnataka) and the Odisha-Jharkhand iron ore belt (Singhbhum, Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj).

 

• Chhattisgarh is one of India's leading iron ore-producing states, largely due to the Bailadila deposits.

 

NOTE

 

• Zinc (Option 2): Major zinc deposits in India are found in Zawar (Rajasthan), not Bailadila.

 

• Bauxite (Option 3): Major bauxite deposits are found in states like Odisha and Jharkhand, not primarily Bailadila.

 

• Manganese (Option 4): Major manganese deposits are found in states like Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Odisha, not primarily Bailadila.

question: The Battle of Karnal is known for the invasion of which of the following aggressors against India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nadir Shah.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Battle of Karnal, fought on 24 February 1739, was a decisive engagement between the invading forces of the Persian ruler Nadir Shah and the Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah. (करनाल का युद्ध — नादिर शाह का आक्रमण)

 

• Nadir Shah decisively defeated the much larger Mughal army, exposing the weakness of the Mughal Empire, and subsequently sacked Delhi, carrying away immense wealth, including the famed Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor diamond.

 

• This battle is regarded as a major turning point that accelerated the decline of the Mughal Empire.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ahmad Shah Abdali (Nadir Shah's former general) later invaded India multiple times and fought the Third Battle of Panipat (1761) against the Marathas.

 

• The immense plunder Nadir Shah took from Delhi is said to have allowed Persia to suspend taxation for several years.

 

NOTE

 

• Nasir Khan (Option 2): Not associated with the Battle of Karnal.

 

• Ahmad Shah Abdali (Option 3): An Afghan invader associated with the Battles of Panipat, not the Battle of Karnal.

 

• Shah Shuja (Option 4): A Mughal prince (son of Shah Jahan), not associated with the Battle of Karnal invasion.
